original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For a closed length-28 word of multiplicity shape (4,4,4,4,4,4,2,2) with a 10-step all-ones arc, prove the short-arc counts are (3,1,1,1,1,1,1,1), the repeated source is a multiplicity-4 source, and the complement counts are (3,3,3,3,3,1,1,1). Record the normalization that replaces the distance-8 identity word by the 120 position triples of that repeated source, with the two doubles chosen among the other seven labels.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one new priced connector operation. This package keeps the published singleton alphabet and records the distance-10 count vector left open by the length-28 all-ones split. It does not add a call or change kappa.
bottleneck_link: A universal length-28 singleton word would show the #5234 floor is sharp and could lower the eight-source query bill. The distance-10 count vector is a necessary shape for one of the four all-ones anchors left unresolved by the 2026-11-11 handoff. It removes the distance-8 normalization, and it does not yet exclude the anchor or price a supplier.
stop_rule: Stop once the distance-10 count vector, the role table, the five complement on-steps, and the 120-form normalization are checked. Do not search complement orders for a universal word, and do not solve distances 12 or 14.
evidence: Written excess argument and role table. The verifier exhausts the 6561 odd tuples in {1,3,5}^8, all 224 multiplicity alignments, all 120 normal forms, and all 4838400 count-type words. A closed witness realizes the role table and 58 prefix differences. Mutations and the distance-8 identity chain are rejected.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: For one of the 120 position triples, which of the 21 double-label pairs have a complement order making the length-28 prefix set a difference basis of F_2^8?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A yes answer would show that an all-ones arc of distance 10 is compatible with a universal length-28 word. A no answer for every pair would remove this anchor from the handoff. The count vector only makes the index finite.
open_questions.first_step: Keep the arc prefixes of positions (0, 1, 2) fixed and apply one adjacent transposition to the recorded complement order, recording whether the difference count rises above 58.
open_questions.blocked_by: The legal orders of that 18-step multiset are still too many for an unpruned listing. One transposition, and any partial search, would not be an exclusion.

open_questions.question: Do the five complement on-steps and the three single off-steps have an empty-quadrant turn-off split?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The distance-8 case-II obligation used the order of two single off-steps. Distance 10 has three sources that turn off only once, so a similar split would be a different statement.
open_questions.first_step: For positions (0, 1, 2) and doubles {1, 2}, name the quadrant sequence created by one order of those three off-steps.
open_questions.blocked_by: The five ordinary quadruples turn back on between those off-steps, so the distance-8 flag table does not apply. This package does not list the orders.

open_questions.question: What replaces the distance-10 count vector at all-ones distances 12 and 14?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The handoff and the distance-8 packages leave those two anchors unresolved. They are separate questions because the positive-odd composition is no longer unique.
open_questions.first_step: Solve the positive-odd composition at that one length in its own package, before any normalization.
open_questions.blocked_by: Excess 1 is the only positive excess for which the distance-10 equation has a unique solution. Changing the number 10 does not prove the longer cases.

claim_type: scoped written proof with exhaustive finite censuses of the named domains
unrun_obligations: No replay of the cited f(7)=24 proof.
No search of complement orders and no universal length-28 word.
No count vector for distance 12 or 14.
No application of the #6966 rank floor or the #7088 flat-step budget.
No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, supplier admission, or kappa change.
